title: Mastering Outbound Prospecting
description: This is a competency-based course designed for the indentured Technical Sales Representative apprentice. Advanced techniques for lead generation, cold calling, and email outreach using Apollo and LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
learning_objectives: Define an ideal customer profile and build a qualified target list from market signals
Use prospecting tools to research an account and its buying committee before outreach
Open, navigate, and recover a cold call, including its predictable objections
Write a multi-touch email sequence that asks for a specific meeting
Qualify an outbound pipeline against a stated framework and decide what to work next
prerequisites: Introduction to Sales (se101), or equivalent sales fundamentals

lessons.title: Ideal Customer Profile and Target Lists
objectives: Define an ideal customer profile and build a qualified target list from market signals

lessons.title: Account Research with Prospecting Tools
objectives: Use prospecting tools to research an account and its buying committee before outreach

lessons.title: Cold Calling: Openers, Flow, and Objections
objectives: Open, navigate, and recover a cold call, including its predictable objections

lessons.title: Email Sequences That Set Meetings
objectives: Write a multi-touch email sequence that asks for a specific meeting

lessons.title: Qualifying an Outbound Pipeline
objectives: Qualify an outbound pipeline against a stated framework and decide what to work next

lessons.title: Project: Run a Two-Week Outbound Campaign

sequencing_rationale: Targeting precedes touching: lessons 2–3 decide who is worth contacting, 4–5 are the two outbound channels themselves, and 6 closes with the discipline that decides what to do with the replies. Calls come before email because the objections a rep hears live are the raw material for the written sequence. SCOPE ASSUMPTIONS: the intake names lead generation, cold calling, email outreach, and two products — Apollo and LinkedIn Sales Navigator — so those two tools are used as the worked examples in lesson 3, taught as representatives of a category rather than as vendor certification, since the catalog competency (D3-S1-C05) is tool-agnostic. Assumed out of scope: CRM data entry and automation, which is se301's subject even though outbound work touches a CRM; social selling as a discipline of its own; and inbound or partner-sourced lead flow, which the intake never mentions. The project is deliberately small in hours (1) because it is a campaign the learner runs against the work already produced in lessons 2–5 rather than new material.
